items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: Answer the following questions.
items.stem: Why do you think the grandmother felt embarrassed to ask someone else to read to her while the narrator was away?
items.answer: The grandmother felt embarrassed because asking someone else would expose her inability to read, making her feel heavily dependent and helpless despite being from a well-off family. It hurt her dignity and self-respect to beg others for a simple task like reading a magazine.

items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: Answer the following questions.
items.stem: Why does the narrator initially laugh at her grandmother’s determination to learn at the age of sixty-two?
items.answer: The narrator initially laughs because she is just a twelve-year-old child who associates learning and school exclusively with young children. Seeing her sixty-two-year-old grandmother—who has grey hair, wrinkled hands, and spends most of her time in the kitchen—wanting to learn the alphabet seemed funny and out of place to her.

items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: Answer the following questions.
items.stem: What significance does the story of Kashi Yatre have in both the grandmother’s life and the story?
items.answer: The story of Kashi Yatre acts as a mirror to the grandmother’s life. Just as the old lady in the novel had an unfulfilled ardent desire to visit Kashi, the grandmother had a deep, unfulfilled desire to be educated and independent. Furthermore, the protagonist’s sacrifice in the novel deeply resonated with the grandmother’s selfless nature. Ultimately, it was her intense urge to read the next episode of Kashi Yatre independently that pushed her to learn the Kannada alphabet.

items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: Answer the following questions.
items.stem: What does the grandmother’s desire to learn the Kannada alphabet reflect about her?
items.answer: Her desire reflects her immense willpower, determination, and progressive mindset. It shows that she values independence and believes that age is not a barrier to acquiring new knowledge. It also highlights her self-discipline and readiness to work hard to achieve her goals.

items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: Answer the following questions.
items.stem: What lessons can we infer from the grandmother’s action of touching the narrator’s feet?
items.answer: The grandmother touching her granddaughter’s feet teaches us the true meaning of respect and humility. It shows that a teacher should be respected regardless of their age or gender. It breaks conventional age hierarchies, highlighting that knowledge and the one who imparts it are worthy of the highest reverence.

items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: Answer the following questions.
items.stem: What does the following line tell us about the broader theme of the story? ‘For a good cause if you are determined, you can overcome any obstacle.’
items.answer: This line is the central theme of the story. It conveys that true determination and a noble purpose can conquer all barriers, be it age, physical limitations, or societal norms. It teaches that one is never too old to learn and improve oneself.

items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: Answer the following questions.
items.stem: How effectively does the story highlight the value of education in supporting personal independence?
items.answer: The story highlights this very effectively by showcasing the grandmother’s deep anguish when she cannot read the magazine in her granddaughter’s absence. Her wealth was of no use in giving her independence; only the ability to read could do that. Her journey from feeling helpless to confidently reading the novel on her own proves that education is the ultimate tool for true personal independence. Vocabulary and Structures in Context I. The expression ‘hide and seek’ is used in the text. This is called a binomial. Binomials are expressions consisting of two words, usually linked by a conjunction like ‘and’ or ‘or’, that are commonly used together in a fixed order. For example: odds and ends, right or wrong. Match the binomials in Column 1 with their meanings in Column 2. You may refer to a dictionary. NODIA PAGE 300 CBSE CLASS 9 ENGLISH R1 The Incident That Changed Everything One day, the narrator had to leave the village for a week to attend a wedding. During her absence, the weekly magazine arrived, but the grandmother could not read it because she had never been to school. She opened the magazine and rubbed her hands over the pictures, but she could not understand what was written. Though she was from a well-off family, she felt entirely helpless and dependent. She was too embarrassed to ask anyone else in the village to read it to her. When the narrator finally returned from the wedding, she was shocked to find her usually strong and happy grandmother in tears. A Firm Determination to Learn Later that night, the grandmother poured her heart out to her granddaughter. She explained that when she was a little girl, education for women was not considered important, and she had lost her mother early, so she never went to school. She expressed her deep regret over being illiterate. She then announced a life-changing decision: she wanted to learn the Kannada alphabet starting the very next day. She set a strict deadline for herself, vowing to read a novel on her own by Saraswati Puja day during the Dassara festival. Initially, the 12-year-old narrator childishly made fun of her grandmother, laughing at the idea of a 62-year-old woman with grey hair and spectacles trying to learn the alphabet. However, the grandmother simply smiled and said, “For learning, there is no age bar.” The Journey of Teaching and Learning The young narrator took on the role of a teacher, and her grandmother became her most dedicated student. The grandmother worked incredibly hard to achieve her goal. She spent hours doing her homework—reading, writing, and repeatedly reciting the alphabet. Her intense willpower and dedication proved her own belief that if someone is determined for a good cause, they can overcome any obstacle. A Heartwarming Resolution When the day of the Dassara festival finally arrived, the grandmother called the narrator to the puja room. To the young girl’s absolute surprise, the grandmother bent down and touched her granddaughter’s feet. In Indian tradition, youngsters touch the feet of their elders, so this was highly unusual. The grandmother beautifully explained that she was not touching the feet of her young granddaughter, but rather paying respect to her teacher who had helped her become independent. As a reward, the narrator gifted her grandmother a newly published copy of the novel ‘Kashi Yatre’. The grandmother looked at it and confidently read the title out loud, proving that her hard work had paid off and she had passed her test with flying colours.

items.stem: SUMMARY A Village, A Magazine, and a Bond The story, written by Sudha Murty, revolves around a 12-year-old girl (the narrator) and her 62-year-old grandmother, Krishtakka. They live in a small village in North Karnataka. In those days, the transport system was quite slow, so the morning newspapers and weekly magazines always arrived a day late. The village people eagerly waited for a weekly magazine called ‘Karmaveera’, which published a serialised novel named ‘Kashi Yatre’, written by a famous Kannada writer, Triveni. The novel was about an old woman who deeply wished to visit Kashi (Varanasi) but eventually gave up her life savings to help a poor orphan girl get married. The grandmother identified strongly with the novel’s main character, as she too had never been to Kashi. Every week, the narrator would read the next episode of the story aloud to her grandmother, who would then discuss it joyfully with her friends. items.section_heading: Do you know?
items.stem: There’s no doubt that... vii. So, to put it in a few words...
items.answer: Topic 1 : It is important to learn a new language apart from your mother tongue For the Topic Learning a new language is very important in today’s global world. It helps us communicate with people from different countries and cultures. Knowing more than one language improves our thinking ability and memory. It also opens better career opportunities, as many jobs require communication skills in different languages. Moreover, learning a new language helps us understand different cultures and perspectives, making us more open-minded. Therefore, learning another language apart from our mother tongue is highly beneficial. Against the Topic Although learning a new language has benefits, it is not necessary for everyone. Many people can succeed in life using only their mother tongue. Learning a new language requires time and effort, which may not be possible for everyone. In many cases, translation tools and technology can help us communicate easily without learning a new language. Also, focusing too much on other languages may reduce our connection with our own culture and language. Hence, learning a new language is not always essential. Topic 2 : Learning can happen only when you are young For the Topic It is often said that learning happens best at a young age. Children have sharper memory and faster understanding abilities. They can easily learn languages, skills, and concepts compared to adults. Young minds are more flexible and open to new ideas. Early learning also builds a strong foundation for future success. Therefore, learning is easier and more effective when we are young. Against the Topic Learning is a lifelong process and does not stop with age. Adults can also learn new skills, languages, and ideas with dedication and practice. In fact, older people often have better focus, discipline, and real-life experience, which helps in understanding things more deeply. Many successful people have achieved great things later in life. So, learning is not limited to youth; it can happen at any stage of life. Writing Task I. items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: She never went to school.
items.stem: Triveni’s novel Kashi Yatre acts as a powerful catalyst in the story. Analyze how this fictional piece of literature profoundly impacted the grandmother’s real-life choices.
items.answer: In the story, literature serves as a powerful instrument of change. Triveni’s novel, Kashi Yatre, follows an old woman who sacrifices her pilgrimage to help an orphan. Krishtakka, the grandmother, deeply resonated with this protagonist because she too had never visited Kashi. Her emotional investment in the serialised novel was so profound that her inability to read it during her granddaughter’s absence caused her intense agony. The psychological distress of rubbing her hands over the unreadable pages sparked a crucial realization. She recognized the crippling nature of illiteracy. Thus, a fictional story became the ultimate catalyst, igniting her fierce determination to learn the Kannada alphabet and transforming her into an independent, literate woman at the age of sixty-two.

items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: She never went to school.
items.stem: Analyze the character of Krishtakka. How does she evolve from a dependent old woman to an empowered and independent reader?
items.answer: Krishtakka is portrayed as a loving, traditional, yet strong-willed woman. Initially, she represents many women of her generation who were deprived of education due to early marriage and prevailing social norms. Though financially secure, she depends on her twelve-year-old granddaughter to read her favorite magazine. However, her character undergoes a remarkable transformation when she faces helplessness. Instead of giving in to self-pity, she shows great determination and proves that age is not a barrier to learning. She humbly accepts her young granddaughter as her teacher and begins to learn reading and writing. By the end of the story, Krishtakka becomes an empowered and self-reliant individual. Her journey shows that strong willpower and determination can break personal and societal barriers.

items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: She never went to school.
items.stem: Imagine you are the twelve-year-old narrator. Write a diary entry expressing your shock and confusion on the day you found your strong grandmother crying, and her surprising request to teach her to read.
items.answer: Wednesday, 14th April 2026 Dear Diary, I am still reeling from what happened today. When I returned from the wedding, I found Ajji in tears. I was completely terrified! I have seen her face the toughest situations without blinking, so seeing her cry was unimaginably shocking. When she poured her heart out later that night, I realized how utterly helpless she felt just because she couldn’t read Karmaveera. I felt a deep pang of guilt for staying away so long. But then, she surprised me even more. She asked me to teach her the Kannada alphabet! I childishly laughed at her grey hair and spectacles, but her fierce determination silenced me. I am now officially a teacher to my own grandmother! Sudha

items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: She never went to school.
items.stem: “For learning, there is absolutely no age bar at all.” Discuss how this profound theme is established in the story, with reference to the grandmother’s actions.
items.answer: The story beautifully dismantles the stereotype that education is strictly meant for the young. When Krishtakka declares her intention to learn the Kannada alphabet at the age of sixty-two, her twelve-year-old granddaughter playfully mocks her physical aging—her grey hair, spectacles, and wrinkled hands. However, the grandmother responds with absolute conviction, stating that for a good cause, willpower can conquer any obstacle, regardless of age. She proves this philosophy through her rigorous routine. She studies tirelessly, doing homework and reciting alphabets with the obedience of a primary school child. By successfully learning to read before the Dassara deadline, she establishes the core theme: the thirst for knowledge and the capacity to learn remain alive at every stage of human life. items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: Sentila observes her mother making pots. What
items.stem: As Sudha Murty (the narrator), draft a short speech to be delivered at a school assembly on the topic “Overcoming Obstacles through Willpower,” using your grandmother’s journey as your primary example.
items.answer: Respected Principal, Teachers, and my dear friends, Today, I want to talk about a superpower we all possess: willpower. We often give up when we face difficulties and blame our circumstances. But I would like to share a story about my first student—my grandmother. At the age of sixty- two, she realized the pain of being illiterate. Instead of accepting it, she decided to learn the Kannada alphabet. When I laughed at her age, she calmly said that there is no age limit for a good cause. For months, she worked harder than any student I know— studying, reciting, and writing continuously. On the occasion of Dassara, she read her first novel on her own. Her journey taught me that no obstacle—whether age, society, or past regrets— can stand against strong determination. Thank you. items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: The narrative includes an element of
items.stem: The relationship between the grandmother and the granddaughter undergoes a beautiful role reversal. Evaluate how this unusual dynamic strengthens their bond.
items.answer: The traditional relationship between a grandparent and a grandchild usually involves the elder teaching the younger. However, in this story, there is an interesting role reversal where a twelve-year-old girl becomes the teacher of her sixty-two-year-old grandmother. At first, the narrator finds this situation amusing and treats it lightly. But as the grandmother shows sincere dedication and determination to learn, the girl begins to develop deep respect for her. The emotional peak occurs when the grandmother touches the girl’s feet in the puja room. She honors her not as a grandchild, but as a Guru who gave her the gift of literacy. This experience transforms their relationship into one based on mutual respect, equality, and affection.

items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: The narrative includes an element of
items.stem: “I knew then that my student had passed with flying colours.” Explain the context of this statement and the significance of this realization by the young teacher.
items.answer: The narrator makes this proud statement on the day of Saraswati Puja. As a reward for her grandmother’s rigorous hard work, the narrator gifts her a newly published copy of the novel Kashi Yatre. The true test of her teaching and the grandmother’s learning culminates in this exact moment. Without any hesitation or assistance, the grandmother opens the book and fluently reads the title and the publisher’s name aloud. For the young teacher, this is a moment of immense triumph. It validates the months of patient teaching and diligent homework. The phrase “passed with flying colours” signifies not just academic success, but the grandmother’s ultimate victory over her deeply rooted dependency, officially marking her successful transition into an independent individual.

items.answer: Krishtakka: (Smiling proudly) “Namaskara, sisters! Have you read the latest episode of Kashi Yatre?” Friend 1: “Not yet, Krishtakka. We are waiting for someone to read it to us. Did Sudha read it to you?” Krishtakka: “No, she didn’t! I read it myself. The old woman in the story finally gave her savings to the orphan girl!” Friend 2: (Astonished) “You read it yourself? But you couldn’t read Kannada!” Krishtakka: “I couldn’t, but my little Sudha taught me. I studied every single day. I was so tired of feeling helpless and relying on others just to follow a story.” Friend 1: “That is incredible, Krishtakka! At our age, learning is so difficult.” Krishtakka: “Age is just a number! If you have the determination, nothing can stop you from gaining independence.”

items.chapter: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
items.section_heading: The narrative includes an element of
items.stem: Imagine you are Krishtakka. Write a letter to the famous author Triveni, expressing your gratitude for her novel and sharing how it inspired you to learn to read.
items.answer: Dear Triveni, I am a sixty-two-year-old woman from a small village in North Karnataka, and I am writing to express my deepest gratitude to you. Your novel, Kashi Yatre, literally changed my life. Like your protagonist, I too had a deep yearning, but mine wasn’t to visit Kashi; it was to escape the suffocating darkness of illiteracy. When I couldn’t read your serialised story during my granddaughter’s absence, I felt an unbearable agony. That helplessness sparked a fire within me. I decided to learn the Kannada alphabet, and my twelve-year-old granddaughter became my teacher. Today, I can proudly read your beautiful novel independently. Thank you for creating a story so compelling that it gave an old woman the courage to reclaim her independence. Yours sincerely, Krishtakka
